subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose the opt-in deferred-maintenance timeout and generic synchronous queue timeout hook, accepting caller-owned fencing and late-worker abandonment as the supported contract?
rationale: The implementation appears coherent and proven, but repository policy reserves new public config and fallback/cancellation semantics for explicit owner judgment, especially where plugin work can outlive lane release.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Land the current compatibility-preserving design with the timeout disabled by default and treat runtime-owned fencing as the supported abandonment boundary.

options.title: Reuse one existing safety budget
options.body: Refactor maintenance onto the existing host compaction timeout contract to avoid a new public setting, after proving that the shared duration and upgrade behavior fit maintenance workloads.

options.title: Pause the core change
options.body: Keep the linked issue open until context-engine owners define a cooperative cancellation or stricter plugin contract that can terminate rather than abandon maintenance.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Land the current compatibility-preserving design with the timeout disabled by default and treat runtime-owned fencing as the supported abandonment boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline explicitly routed this context-engine/session contract decision to jalehman, and no stronger current-main decision-owner signal is available.
